title: Mapping-simplex quasi-equivalences are categorical equivalences after arbitrary base change
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, standard simplices and degreewise pullbacks from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], cartesian fibrations and cartesian edges from [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], categorical equivalences from [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure], and the marked mapping simplex $M^m(A)$ from [lem-coef-cartesian-mapping-simplex-presentation]. Let $n\geq0$, let $p:Y\to\Delta^n$ be a cartesian fibration with $Y$ small, and let $A_0\leftarrow\cdots\leftarrow A_n$ be a chain of small simplicial sets. Suppose $q:M^m(A)\to Y$ is a simplicial map over $\Delta^n$, takes every edge $(\alpha,a)$ with $a$ degenerate to a $p$-cartesian edge, and induces a categorical equivalence $A_i\to Y\times_{\Delta^n}\{i\}$ for each $0\leq i\leq n$. For every small simplicial set $T$ and every simplicial map $t:T\to\Delta^n$, the induced map of underlying simplicial sets
$$q_T:M^m(A)\times_{\Delta^n}T\longrightarrow Y\times_{\Delta^n}T$$
is a categorical equivalence. Neither $T$ nor the $A_i$ are required to be quasicategories, and $t$ need not be injective. Empty simplicial sets and $n=0$ are included.
